package_info.why_malicious: Multiple XSS vulnerabilities in the FigCaption widget and widget handling allow attackers to inject arbitrary HTML, attributes, and classes, bypassing sanitization and enabling stored and self-XSS, page defacement, and user redirection. These flaws break the expected HTML sandboxing and can be exploited by low-privileged users.

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side, stored in DB, rendered in page body)
required_permissions: potential network (if exfiltrating data via XSS)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: <figcaption class="cke_widget_editable" data-placeholder="Enter caption here" data-cke-widget-editable="caption" data-cke-enter-mode="2" data-cke-filter="46" data-cke-display-name="caption" contenteditable="true">I am a caption</figcaption>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At content creation and page render, the code allows arbitrary HTML and attributes in the figcaption, which are then rendered in the DOM, enabling injection of malicious content or attributes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allows injection of arbitrary HTML and attributes into a context that is rendered as part of the page, breaking containment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict HTML and attributes to a safe whitelist; here, arbitrary attributes and classes are allowed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use would be to style captions or add semantic markup, but not to inject arbitrary classes or data attributes.
key_indicators: Ability to inject arbitrary classes and data-* attributes

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side, stored in DB, rendered in page body)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At content creation and page render, the code injects a link with a class that covers the entire page, causing all user clicks to redirect to an attacker-controlled site.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting a class that covers the entire UI and redirects users is a clear defacement and phishing vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal captions should not be able to overlay or hijack the entire UI.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Overlay classes are used in legitimate modals, but not in user-generated captions.

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side, stored in DB, rendered in page body)
required_permissions: potential network (if XSS payload exfiltrates data)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At content creation and page render, the code injects an tag with a javascript: URL, which can trigger a JavaScript payload if the browser allows it.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting javascript: URLs in src attributes is a classic XSS vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal sanitization should strip or block javascript: URLs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; images should never use javascript: URLs.
key_indicators: Presence of javascript: scheme in src attribute

execution_context.file_location: CKEditor instance in Drupal content editor (client-side, preview mode)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When previewing content, the code injects a <script> tag that executes arbitrary JavaScript, resulting in self-XSS.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct injection and execution of <script> tags in preview mode is a clear XSS vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Preview mode should sanitize and block script execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; script tags should never be allowed in user content.
key_indicators: Execution of arbitrary JavaScript in preview mode
Lack of sanitization in preview rendering

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts malicious HTML payload using FigCaption or widget attributes (e.g., with arbitrary classes, javascript: URLs, or <script> tags).
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is stored in Drupal content database.

attack_chain.action: Payload is rendered in the CKEditor instance or on the public-facing page, triggering DOM manipulation or script execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: XSS, page defacement, or user redirection.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the victim's browser, potentially hijacking sessions, redirecting users, or exfiltrating data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Account compromise, phishing, or further exploitation.

behavioral_signatures: User-generated content containing <script> tags or javascript: URLs in attributes
Presence of overlay classes (e.g., joyride-modal-bg) in user content
Arbitrary data-* attributes or classes in figcaption or widget HTML
file_indicators: Content fields in the Drupal database containing <script>, javascript:, or suspicious class names
Unusual attributes in
network_indicators: Unexpected outbound requests triggered by user interaction with content (e.g., redirection to external domains)
JavaScript execution resulting in network requests to attacker-controlled domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan user-generated content for <script> tags, javascript: URLs, and suspicious classes or data-* attributes in figcaption and widget HTML. Monitor rendered pages for DOM elements with overlay classes or unexpected attributes. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block known XSS payloads and monitor for suspicious outbound network activity originating from user interaction with content.
